📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, it’s been a rough year for travel. Oil prices skyrocketed after Iran closed the Strait of Hormuz at the start of the U.S.-Israeli war on the country, leaving many people thinking twice about the steep cost of airfare. More recent disruptions, including to U.S. air traffic control, made us determined to curate a list of holiday gift recommendations that will make you feel globally connected from the comfort of your own home.

Sources indicate that so Brick your phone, set tea to steep with a gooseneck kettle, put on a Mongolian cashmere hoodie, and cozy up to complete a British paint-by-numbers kit while munching on Spanish jamón chips. (Fear not: Those still inclined to travel will also find our favorite bags and gadgets.).

According to recent reports, it’s been a rough year for travel. Oil prices skyrocketed after Iran closed the Strait of Hormuz at the start of the U.S.-Israeli war on the country, leaving many people thinking twice about the steep cost of airfare. More recent disruptions, including to U.S. air traffic control, made us determined to curate a list of holiday gift recommendations that will make you feel globally connected from the comfort of your own home.

According to recent reports, so Brick your phone, set tea to steep with a gooseneck kettle, put on a Mongolian cashmere hoodie, and cozy up to complete a British paint-by-numbers kit while munching on Spanish jamón chips. (Fear not: Those still inclined to travel will also find our favorite bags and gadgets.).

Baggu Medium Nylon Crescent Bag ($56).

I’ll be the first to admit that I have a massive problem—er, a bag problem. My closet is practically overflowing with thrifted purses, and my FP colleagues know that I come into the office carrying not one or two sensible totes, but three or four. So trust me when I say that I know bags, and this one stands above the rest.

Recent findings suggest that baggu’s Medium Nylon Crescent Bag is a workhorse, ideal for a friend or loved one looking for a trusty companion for weekend errands, jet-setting adventures, and everything in between. I’ve previously recommended Baggu’s packing cubes for their durability and cute patterns. This product has those same qualities.

Sleek and roomy, the crescent bag is available in a range of colors, materials (mine is leather), and sizes, although I’ve found that the medium-sized pouch is perfect for my needs.

JisuLife Portable Handheld Fan Ultra2 ($72.67, at the moment on sale).

According to recent reports, I’ve traveled to a bunch of countries over the years, but my luggage tag collection is not the largest at FP—not by a long shot. Many of my colleagues have been to more destinations and stayed longer, just one of the things that makes working here so delightful. In the office, everyone has a travel tip.

According to recent reports, mine: The gadgets you take with you should be multifunctional. The exemplar of an all-purpose gadget is this freakishly powerful fan that’s also a power bank, flashlight, and handy-dandy keyboard cleaner. I keep it in my carry-on, fan myself before takeoff, charge my phone over the Atlantic, and light up the seat pocket on arrival to make sure I didn’t leave my passport behind. As for my keyboard—it’s reliably crumb-free.

Etnodim Ivory Wool Scarf “Zavii” ($122).

Sources indicate that etnodim makes high-quality, gorgeous interpretations of classical Ukrainian clothes, from embroidered shirts and dresses to traditional kerchiefs. On a trip to Kyiv this fall, I got a traditional shirt, known as a vyshyvanka, for my daughter from their brand store in Podil, Kyiv’s equivalent of Brooklyn. Fortunately, you don’t have to travel 30-plus hours by plane and train to get their items, which are also sold online.

While I’d heartily recommend Etnodim’s wildly colorful designs, their more basic items—like this merino wool scarf—go with anything. Best of all, you’ll be supporting a Ukrainian brand that celebrates the country’s unique identity, in opposition to Russia’s best efforts to stamp out such cultural expressions.

Breville Milk Café milk frother ($199.95).

Industry observers note that after realizing just how much money I was spending per month on lattes at my local (international chain) coffee shop, I decided to look into making them at home. But I didn’t want to spend thousands of dollars on some behemoth machine that requires a specialist degree to operate, either.

Enter the Breville Milk Café milk frother. It’s super easy to use and clean, it doesn’t take up much counter space, and it reliably makes the perfect steamed milk to my desired temperature and amount of foam. I’ve used it at least once—if not twice—a day for the last five months, and it hasn’t let me down yet.

Recent findings suggest that but that’s just the milk part of the equation. Now on to the coffee part….

Breville Nespresso Original Essenza Mini Espresso Machine ($174.99).

The Nespresso Original Essenza Mini Espresso Machine is basically a Keurig for espresso. You don’t have to grind beans or fiddle with a million buttons and levers to make a single shot of espresso—just pop in a Nespresso pod; make sure the little, easily removable water tank in the back is full; and hit a button.

According to recent reports, this machine is also compact, so it doesn’t monopolize your kitchen. Best of all, the espresso tastes just as rich and creamy as it would if you went to the corner coffee shop—and you don’t even have to put on pants to enjoy it.

—Jennifer Williams, deputy editor.

Ortlieb Vario Lite pannier backpack ($195).

It has been revealed that FP recently moved offices to a space farther away from the D.C. Metro’s Red Line—and so I became a bike commuter.

According to recent reports, biking has long been my preferred mode of transportation on the weekends, when I shuttle between yoga and Trader Joe’s with the help of a storage basket. But I promptly realized that commuting is an entirely different ball game. Laptop plus lunch is a heavy—and valuable—combo. I did not trust my basket, however adorable, to keep these items secure.

Enter: a pannier backpack. Rather than settling either for a backpack (which would strain my back while biking and probably make me sweaty) or a pannier (which would be difficult to transport after parking my bike), I decided to invest in this brilliant product from Ortlieb, a German brand that happens to be—like me—Franconian. It has transformed my commute.

It has been revealed that the Vario Lite allows me to toggle seamlessly between pannier and backpack modes. It has an interior laptop pocket and outer compartment where I store my keys and phone for easy access. Its rolltop structure means that its size is flexible, and its backpack function is ergonomic. Did I mention that it’s waterproof, too?

The Vario Lite is the little brother of the Vario, a slightly larger pannier backpack from Ortlieb. I tried on both and found the Vario Lite to be a better fit on my 5’1” frame. But anyone can rest assured that there’s an entire line of high-quality pannier backpacks—in a range of colors—to choose from.

Brick Phone Distraction Blocker ($56.80, right now on sale).

The Brick—a magnetic square you can use to curtail access to your phone—is an invention I resisted for a long time. Its very existence was proof that we were living at capitalism’s nadir: You’re telling me I need to buy a little plastic brick to blunt the pernicious effects of this other little plastic brick?

And yet. The Brick has made my life better, and here are the numbers to back up that claim. Before acquiring the device, I was averaging 10 hours and 40 minutes on my phone per day. Now that number is down to just under eight hours. Sometimes, when there isn’t an international spy scandal all over the news, it has been known to hit seven.

That I have been wasting this much of my life scrolling is mortifying enough. What’s worse is how easy it was to break the habit. The minor inconvenience the Brick depends on is that once you block certain apps you can only unblock them by tapping your phone to the cube. Tapping the cube is very easy. But most of the time, it’s simply too much of a bother. So instead of doomscrolling, you put down the phone and do something else instead, such as engaging with your children or animals.

Turns out you can throw money at seemingly intractable problems. Capitalism, you win this round.

Scotch Precision Ultra Edge Scissors ($11.39).

I, too, initially recommended the Brick (above) but voluntarily scrapped my write-up lest attention spans wane while reading too many words about a plastic square. Instead, I’d like to recommend something analogue to fill your newfound free time: paper collage.

According to recent reports, I recently turned to physical collaging as a cathartic supplement to the digital work I sometimes do for FP. It’s the perfect hobby for the world traveler with piles of ephemera or magazine readers with a backlog of vintage Foreign Policy and National Geographic. Pull together a gift collage kit with paper bits of your choice and these sharp, precise scissors.

These superior snips come recommended secondhand by Ray Orr, a collage artist and former visual journalist and co-founder of Living Room DC, a creative space in D.C.’s Mount Pleasant neighborhood. Consider gifting a workshop or drop-in session for collage or artmaking in the cozy spot.

—Lori Kelley, executive creative director.

Cocinare FLOW B9 Gooseneck Electric Kettle ($55.99, currently on sale).

It has been revealed that you know what they say: A warm cup of tea a day keeps the geopolitical crises away. Or maybe two cups, given the present outlook. Actually, scratch that—might be best to have three.

It has been revealed that world leaders may have decided to shirk responsibility for confronting our warming planet, but you can still control the temperature of water at home with this luxurious electric kettle. No software required; this baby does not run on Outlook. Just plug the kettle in, set it to the optimal steeping temperature for your beverage of choice, and hit the button. A quiet moment with a perfectly warmed cup of tea is just minutes away. (For a slightly less precise but more budget-friendly option, consider this alternative.).

Everyman’s Library Pocket Classics ($16-$28).

If you’re like me, packing for a trip is a calculation of how much reading material you can bring to fill time spent in transit without losing precious real estate in your bag. “They’ll have bookstores there,” a wise friend once reminded me. But a smart traveler comes prepared!

Short story collections from Penguin Random House’s Everyman’s Library Pocket Classics Series are a compact travel companion and a great gift for someone you know who’s getting excited for an upcoming trip (or still reminiscing about their last one).

From India to Russia to Ireland, these anthologies compile literary short stories and book excerpts related to the featured country, continent, or city. Their contents can introduce you to a new destination, deepen your appreciation for a place you already love, or even inspire a change of itinerary.

I’ve found the anthology format to be ideal for the random stretches of time to kill when traveling between destinations. The stories are just the right length to digest on a plane, bus, or train ride, and can even make the inevitable delay more enjoyable.

Zeedog Ruff Leash ($15.20, right now on sale).

This year, I became the owner of a young dog—and also the continued owner of pair of aging arms. After having my shoulder wrenched by my puppy’s eagerness to chase D.C.’s rats a few too many times, I switched to this leash from Zeedog.

It has been revealed that through a simple shock-absorbing design, which looks like a stretchy wave at the end of the leash, the Ruff Leash absorbs the force when your dog yanks. It also comes, like puppies, in a stylish variety of colors. Strongly recommended for anyone foolish enough, like me, to get one.

Sony WH-1000XM6 Noise-Canceling Headphones ($348, at the moment on sale).

According to recent reports, living in a loud city like New York, I’ve long been a believer in a good pair of headphones. Even before advances in noise-canceling technology, hearing the Talking Heads instead of the roar of an oncoming subway was an amazing way to mitigate the sounds of crowded urban life.

Sources indicate that recently, I upgraded from my older Sony headphones to the latest WH-1000XM6s. What they lack in catchy brand naming, they make up for in incredible sound quality and call clarity. From Zoom calls to catching background noise in video edits, they sound incredible while blocking out everything I don’t want to hear.

—Connor Curfman, staff designer.

Hebe Studio Paint By Numbers Kit ($57).

I’ve long admired the bold colors and vibrant, travel-inspired scenes painted by Rhi James, the U.K. artist behind Hebe Studio. Her paint-by-numbers kits offer a delightfully nostalgic way to slow down and create beautiful artwork of your own. With these kits—which are designed to be beginner-friendly and include high-quality paints, brushes, and canvas—it’s easy to feel confident as you bring your masterpiece to life. James’s enchanting landscapes are a unique gift that will add a personal touch to someone’s home while also giving them a creative escape.

—Sara Stewart, senior creative director, product.

Quince Mongolian Cashmere Pullover Hoodie ($99.90).

Whether or not you’re comfortable thinking of yourself as the kind of person who wears a cashmere pullover hoodie, you will feel comfortable wearing a cashmere pullover hoodie. Quince cashmere is responsibly and sustainably sourced, so you can also feel comfortable about the conditions of the goat whose soft, soft hair you are wearing. This makes a great gift for anyone whose head gets jealous when they put on a sweater.

Schoolhouse x Pendleton Abington Hall Throw ($139.99-$238.99, currently on sale).

Industry observers note that as winter approaches, there’s nowhere I want to be but snuggled under a blanket and sitting by a crackling fire. I grew up in the woods of the Pacific Northwest and, to me, Pendleton is the height of luxury. Since 1909, this Oregon-based mill has been producing wool blankets and textiles to outfit lumberjacks and the Beach Boys alike. Pendleton’s collaboration with home goods brand Schoolhouse marries its heritage product with modern style. This 100 percent wool, “Made in USA” blanket is sure to elevate any cozy space and keep you warm all winter long.

—Rylie Munn, social media editor.

A confession: I have long known what the perfect holiday gift is, but I’ve kept it to myself. No more! It’s a puzzle from Liberty Puzzles, a wooden jigsaw puzzle made in Boulder, Colorado. (Full disclosure: I worked at Liberty Puzzles long ago, but unlike my friends at fast-food joints, who came away swearing off the menu, I left charmed having seen how the product gets made.).

It has been revealed that what sets a Liberty Puzzle apart from the typical cardboard variety? For starters, the shapes. Each one is unusual, and thick, laser-cut pieces fall into place with a satisfying click. They also have a faint smell of burnt maple. Best of all, if you ever lose a piece—say, in the stomach of a mischievous furry friend—the company will replace it for free.

Sources indicate that the catalog is quite global, including landscapes, art, maps, and vintage posters, so there’s something for everyone. I’ll make it easy for you: A gastronomical map of Italy for the couple fresh back from their honeymoon! A woodblock print of Japan’s snow-dusted Mount Haruna for the burgeoning snowboarder! A painting of Diana and her nymphs for the Roman history buff in your life! They even make kids’ puzzles.

Torres Selecta Iberian Ham Gourmet Potato Chips ($49).

Give the candy canes a break this year and stuff your stockings with chips!

I first encountered these pork-flavored potato chips at my neighborhood wine bar years ago, and they promptly became a cult favorite. They’ve been on my mind again, having recently returned from Andalusia, Spain, where jamón ibérico seemed to show up at every meal.

It has been revealed that salty, savory, and downright decadent, these chips would pair great with a dollop of creme fraiche; a dab of fig jam, pickled shallots, or salmon roe; and a glass of cava. They’re the perfect treat for the adventurous eater on your list, or anyone who’s still dreaming of their last trip.

—Megan DuBois, associate editor.

Mens Soft Fleece Drawstring Elastic Waist Cargo Pants ($16.97).

Yes, you read that right: I’m recommending sweatpants.

It has been revealed that my travel frequency has gone up a lot this year (not a complaint!), and I’ve put a lot of thought into what I wear on long flights. Cargo sweatpants have been a game-changer for comfort and convenience. The additional pockets are useful for carrying chargers, chewing gum, and other paraphernalia without constantly having to open the overhead bin. And the pockets have buttons to close them, so I avoid the constant fear of losing my passport. The sweatpants are also possibly the most comfortable item of clothing I own.

While I purchased my pair at a brick-and-mortar store in India (shout-out to Marks & Spencer), I’m sure this equivalent on Amazon is just as good. Having closed pockets is the key. And these sweatpants cost less than some Manhattan cocktails, so you can pick up a few to keep in rotation.

Bic 4-Color Original Retractable Ballpoint Pen ($4.38, currently on sale).

Industry observers note that one of the dangers of having kids is the constant temptation to indulge in nostalgia for the objects of one’s own youth. But sometimes nostalgia can be an invitation to genuine rediscovery.

Recent findings suggest that such was my experience with the classic Bic four-color pen. I bought one for my fifth-grade son during this year’s back-to-school run-up and watched as his newfound power dawned. You’re writing in blue, and with a flick of the thumb: Boom! Green. If the mood strikes: Boom! Back to blue—or red?

I soon bought a four-color pen for myself and rapidly came to a renewed appreciation for its simple design and small daily offer of variety. But reading about the pen’s history also gave me a deeper understanding of its geopolitical significance. I hadn’t known that Bic is a French company, and that the iconic four-color pen has always—since its original release in 1970—been a product proudly made in France. The factory in the town of Montévrain still closely guards its manufacturing secrets.

The Bic four-color pen isn’t just a writing implement—it’s a precisely engineered machine, an enduring symbol of Francofuturism. All of which makes it the perfect stocking stuffer for the status-conscious middle schooler in your life—or the wonky Europhilic aesthete.

The Oregon Trail Card Game ($18.50).

It has been revealed that although I have never been much of a video gamer, I would be lying if I stated that the 1990s classic Oregon Trail did not eat up hours of my childhood. Fighting to survive bandits, broken axels, and (of course) dysentery was a favorite activity of mine when the days were cold, the nights were long, and I needed an escape from our chaotic world.

So when I was gifted a physical version of the iconic game, I was hooked. The story is the same: Make your way from Independence, Missouri, to Willamette Valley, Oregon, without succumbing to drowning, starvation, or a host of other calamities. My friends and I have spent hours around my coffee table attempting to cross the treacherous 2,000-plus-mile passage without incident. There have been screaming matches, thrown cards, and more typhoid outbreaks than we can count.

And, of course, we have died every time.

—Alexandra Sharp, World Brief writer.

An FP Insider Gift Subscription and Limited-Edition Tote Bag ($124.50 with code HOLIDAY50).

In a recent development, the best gift for an independent thinker in your life is one year of Foreign Policy. This holiday season, an annual FP Insider gift subscription includes a limited-edition FOREIGN POLICY tote, made from durable heavyweight cotton canvas with an external side pocket. Plus: ad-free reading and behind-the-scenes dispatches from FP’s stable of geopolitical experts. Visit our gift subscriptions page for more information. Want this tote for yourself? Join or upgrade to Insider to unlock VIP membership perks.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Eric Schiffer, CEO of Reputation Management Consultants Inc., believes Democrats are engaging in double-sided messaging by attacking Trump’s efforts to reinstate Jensen Huang.

The Trump administration’s efforts to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO of Nvidia have set a latest bar for shaping a private corporation, according to Eric Schiffer, chairman and CEO of Reputation Management Consultants, a crisis management and brand protection firm.

"Trump came in to really give a second life to Jensen, where he would have been dead," Schiffer told Fox News Digital Tuesday.

Schiffer said the intervention has opened a kind of Pandora’s box that Democrats may seek to exploit to benefit ideological allies in the private sector. Still, he said the national security interests underpinning Trump’s efforts to intervene on behalf of Huang fall within the responsibilities of the presidency.

JENSEN HUANG'S NVIDIA RETURN SENDS CHINA A CLEAR MESSAGE: THE AI RACE IS ON.

Jensen Huang apologized to Nvidia employees for being unfaithful to his wife, saying his actions hurt her and their children and that "there is no excuse for what I did." (Soeren Stache/picture alliance/Getty Images).

Asked whether he believes Democrats may use the moment as a precedent to tip the scales in favor of ideological allies down the road, Schiffer stated he sees that possibility in the cards.

Recent findings suggest that "I think that, of course, they would have that capability. I think that that is a risk," Schiffer said.

But Schiffer mentioned the justification would likely depend on the circumstances.

"If the Democrats had a similar situation or it's a leading organization that is so critical to both national security and the economy, then it would make sense," Schiffer stated.

In a recent development, "However, if the Democrats — and perhaps the future president that might be a Democrat — is empowering a crony … then I think they're going to be open to significant criticism. And I think that there would be pushback on behalf of the American public," he added.

"This is very unique and different in my opinion.".

CHINA COULD EXPLOIT US TECHNOLOGY TO THREATEN AMERICAN FORCES, CONGRESSIONAL WATCHDOG LEADERS WARN.

In a recent development, president Donald Trump stands with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang after presenting him with the National Medal of Science during a summit at the U.S. Institute of Peace, renamed The Donald J. Trump Institute of Peace by the Trump administration, in Washington, D.C., Oct. 8, 2026. (Reuters/Evan Vucci).

Industry observers note that nvidia's board decided to bring back Huang as CEO after he resigned earlier this month following reports of an extramarital relationship with Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive. The Latest York Times reported U.S. intelligence identified Alice Huang as a suspected Chinese intelligence asset operating under corporate cover.

A source familiar with the matter told Fox News that President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance worked over the weekend to reinstate Huang after they received security briefings and became convinced that Huang did not present a national security threat in his role as CEO.

In recent days, Vance worked with figures in Silicon Valley and executives at Nvidia to urge the board to reinstate him, the source stated.

In a recent development, democrats have blasted Trump's involvement, calling it presidential overreach. Rep. Robert Garcia, D-Calif., the top Democrat on the House Oversight Committee, noted that Trump owns Nvidia stock. Trump holds between $13 million and $62 million in Nvidia stock, according to reporting from The Washington Post and its review of Trump's disclosures.

Recent findings suggest that "We must investigate these actions. No president who has invested in a private tech giant should be involved in their board decisions," Garcia mentioned in a statement.

U.S. House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-Calif., echoed Garcia's criticisms.

"We will not allow America’s national security to be sold out by the Trump Administration for personal financial gain," Jeffries wrote in a press release on Monday.

Despite those criticisms from Democrats, Schiffer believes the nation’s security interests prevailed through Trump’s decision, arguing that Nvidia's central role in U.S. competition with China made Huang’s return a matter the president could not ignore.

According to recent reports, "[In] the office of the presidency, you know, there's the duty to ensure that the United States continues to be strong geopolitically and certainly from a national security perspective. The move to help Jensen accomplishes those," Schiffer noted.

"That's part of what a good leader and a strong leader should be doing.".

TO BEAT CHINA ON AI, WASHINGTON MUST FIRST EARN AMERICANS' TRUST.

President Donald Trump speaks with Elon Musk and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang during the Saudi Investment Forum at the Kennedy Center Nov. 19, 2025, in Washington. (AP Photo/Evan Vucci).

Apart from its reasoning for the administration's intervention, Schiffer pointed out that Trump had only used soft power to encourage Huang's return, a far cry from forcing Nvidia into its decision through any formal use of the presidency.

"This was not a situation where the government came in under some military policy and tried to take control of Nvidia," Schiffer said. "This was the lightest form of power.".

The White House and the Office of the Vice President did not immediately respond to requests for comment about whether they shared concerns about Democrats using political power to intervene in the private sector in future administrations or whether the administration had created a latest precedent for corporate intervention.

Leo Briceno is a politics reporter for the congressional team at Fox News Digital. He was previously a reporter with World Magazine.

Don’t Let China Hawks Exploit the Nvidia Scandal

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Get audio access with any FP subscription.

Amid the flurry of commentary over Nvidia and Jensen Huang’s “gone today, here tomorrow” act, there is one question that remains undiscussed: Has U.S. policy toward China succeeded in its aims of maintaining American preeminence and security?

It has been revealed that the overwhelming reaction to Huang’s reinstatement has been bipartisan outrage at U.S. President Donald Trump’s interference in a private firm, coupled with demands for stricter enforcement of U.S. export controls on the sale of Nvidia’s chips to China. As Sen. Tom Cotton mentioned, “I have warned the administration from the start about Communist China obtaining our most advanced chips through both smuggling and remote access.”.

Recent findings suggest that amid the flurry of commentary over Nvidia and Jensen Huang’s “gone today, here tomorrow” act, there is one question that remains undiscussed: Has U.S. policy toward China succeeded in its aims of maintaining American preeminence and security?

Sources indicate that the overwhelming reaction to Huang’s reinstatement has been bipartisan outrage at U.S. President Donald Trump’s interference in a private organization, coupled with demands for stricter enforcement of U.S. export controls on the sale of Nvidia’s chips to China. As Sen. Tom Cotton remarked, “I have warned the administration from the start about Communist China obtaining our most advanced chips through both smuggling and remote access.”.

Recent findings suggest that that sentiment is widely shared. But should it be?

According to recent reports, there was a point sometime in the mid-2010s when U.S. policy shifted decisively from engaging China to containing it. This began during U.S. President Barack Obama’s second term, and then it accelerated with the first tariff war and the campaign against Huawei during the first season of the Trump show. It was cemented as consensus policy during the U.S. President Joe Biden’s interregnum and has been maintained during the second season of Trump.

This shift was driven by a growing consensus that engagement had failed. China’s entry into the World Trade Organization in 2001 was supposed to make it more democratic and open. It did not. China under President Xi Jinping instead turned away from political reforms, silencing any hint of opposition to the Chinese Communist Party (CCP). Internationally, Beijing adopted a more confrontational stance toward the United States while continuing to steal American intellectual property.

In a recent development, in this context, Washington embraced export controls on high-end technology that could enhance the Chinese military or give Chinese companies an edge in the race for preeminence in artificial intelligence. But instead of meaningfully containing or slowing China, these export controls have only succeeded in raising tensions and increasing the potential of a future war.

By most informed accounts, the restrictions in place since 2022 have delayed or impaired the ability of Chinese companies to build AI frontier models on the scale, scope, and speed of Anthropic or OpenAI. The restrictions on semiconductor manufacturing equipment sales to China have also created supply constraints that have pressured the Chinese military.

As a result, however, China has become far more self-reliant and aggressively built out its own domestic chip design and manufacturing. Though these domestic efforts lag behind the United States, Nvidia, and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Manufacturer by months or even a few years, this has not prevented dramatic breakthroughs such as the unveiling of China’s AI model DeepSeek.

Recent findings suggest that what’s more, China has managed to evade export controls and obtain high-end chips, either through third parties and other countries in Southeast Asia or through good old-fashioned theft and copying. If Nvidia knowingly and purposely evaded those controls with the acquiescence of some in the Trump administration, that remains a profound scandal. But the reality is that even without this kind of corruption, sanctions have consistently failed to prevent countries from accessing things that are available worldwide, even highly controlled military equipment. A country as large and as intertwined with the global economy as China simply cannot be cut off for long.

According to recent reports, by trying to control China’s chip access and only partly succeeding, Washington has pushed Beijing into a more unequivocally hostile stance. The CCP and Xi perceived, rightly, that the United States had no intention of allowing its peaceful rise and concluded that confrontation was inevitable.

According to recent reports, especially in the past two years, Washington also began to cut off China’s access to aspects of the domestic U.S. market. The Trump administration has blocked Chinese attempts to purchase U.S. companies and prevented thousands of Chinese students from studying at American universities. Students and investments both made China more dependent on and integrated with the United States.

Sources indicate that but many Americans, drawing the wrong lessons from the brief period of Japanese ascendency in the late 1980s, saw these developments as a sign of American weakness, not strength. Japan’s investment in Rockefeller Center and Pebble Beach actually bound the country more closely to the United States and in the process demonstrated how attractive and singular U.S. properties and capital markets were (and are). Instead of recognizing this, policymakers simply carried their aversion to foreign investment over to China.

According to recent reports, in the past year, both the Trump administration and Xi seem to have established what was termed “mutually assured disruption.” China can withhold rare-earth exports that are vital to tech companies everywhere, while Washington can use trade restrictions to squeeze the China export machine. The result has been a period of relative calm in U.S.-China tensions.

Now, with the Nvidia drama, that modus vivendi is in question on Capitol Hill. Congress sees the complicity of the White House as a political opening that it can exploit to double down on its preferred strategy of strangling Chinese technological growth.

But the calls for greater export controls and more scrutiny of trade will not make the United States economically or militarily more secure. They will instead push China ever deeper into its adversarial stance. In this new climate, any vestiges of bilateral engagement will be harder to sustain, aggravating the relationship that will determine the stability of the global system over the next decades.

Industry observers note that there is still time to pursue a better policy. From the outset, Washington should have loosened controls on high-end chip exports, which could have helped ease Xi and the CCP’s iron grip on China and soothe bilateral tensions over time. The refrain that the United States can’t afford to let China win the race for artificial general intelligence is grounded in the same fallacy that any country could contain such a technology and that there is some magical first-mover advantage. There certainly wasn’t with any prior technology, nuclear weapons included.

A more sensible and open policy on chip exports remains the best path going forward. Congress can still pursue it, even as it seeks to hold Trump accountable for any corrupt acts—and Huang for any mistakes he may have made. Nvidia’s scandals do not prove that engagement was wrong and should not preclude the United States and China from developing a more cooperative relationship. Global peace should not be sacrificed on account of Huang’s actions, or Trump’s.

Zachary Karabell is the author of the Edgy Optimist Substack and an opinion contributor at the Washington Post.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., attends a news conference with members of the Congressional Progressive Caucus in the Capitol in January. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

Recent findings suggest that A federal judge Monday released more than 160 pages related to the search of Rep. Ilhan Omar’s home last month, detailing a week-long court effort from the federal government to secure the documents.

According to recent reports, judge James Boasberg for the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia ordered the documents unsealed Monday as part of a lawsuit brought by news organizations and an advocacy group seeking to unseal the records related to the search.

The records unsealed Monday show the government first sought a search warrant in the case on Oct. 2, 10 days before the Trump administration eventually secured the warrant. Dozens of the 169 pages released Monday were redacted entirely. Others contained significant redactions which made much of them unreadable.

Industry observers note that the records show that the presiding judge in the case, U.S. Magistrate Judge Matthew J. Sharbaugh, questioned the government about how it would handle the “Speech or Debate implications” of the search.

The Speech or Debate Clause is a provision of the Constitution which gives sitting members of Congress immunity from being charged or even having to testify about anything dealing with “speech or debate” in Congress.

The unsealed document states the government does not think the investigation touches on Omar’s work as a member of Congress at all, and engaged in a weeklong back-and-forth with Sharbaugh about what, if any, alterations to make to the search warrant.

“The United States believes that ILHAN has committed [REDACTED] crimes over decades — beginning long before she was ever in Congress,” one government motion included in the documents indicates.

According to recent reports, eventually, Sharbaugh granted the search warrant on Oct. 9, seeking records, electronics and a cell phone related to the undisclosed charges. But the warrant also contained an order allowing Omar to assert her speech or debate immunity before the government could search what it seized in the warrant, according to the documents disclosed Monday.

Sources indicate that “But the issue that remains and the issue this Court independently raised with the government after its initial review of the warrant application is whether the search of a sitting Member of Congress’ residence implicates the Speech or Debate Clause. The government says no. This Court sees it differently,” Sharbaugh says in an Oct. 9 order.

The documents also noted that the government notified the office of the House Counsel, which stated there could be no Speech or Debate protection for a member’s private residence.

Sources indicate that the government’s filings in the case suggested that they are looking for evidence of crimes that may have occurred as early as 1980, around the time Omar was born. The documents unsealed Monday do not include the nature of the crimes the government is investigating.

Separately Monday,  the DOJ opposed releasing information from a second suit filed by Omar seeking return of items taken by agents during the search without further briefing.

“Ultimately, if the Press Applicants want access to the Separate Docket, the Court should require them to file papers showing why they’re entitled to it,” the filing indicates.

In a recent development, the administration executed the search warrant last month ahead of the elections, drawing criticism from Democrats and outside experts that the decision was made for political reasons. Since the search, administration officials have said there is a criminal investigation into Omar, tied to her immigration into the United States as a child.

After ruling last week that some records could be unsealed, Boasberg said the press organizations and advocacy group could still seek to unseal more records.

Tech Report: La última oportunidad para la paz

💡 Key Takeaways

  • En algún momento de la última década, el mundo empezó a aceptar la guerra como algo inevitable.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

PEDRO SÁNCHEZ es presidente del Gobierno de España.

Cómo evitar otra guerra mundial.

En algún momento de la última década, el mundo empezó a aceptar la guerra como algo inevitable. Las guerras de agresión, como las de Ucrania, el Líbano o Irán, aumentan y siembran horror, ruina y el temor a una confrontación global. Los gobiernos piensan cada vez más en la guerra como algo para lo que hay que prepararse y presupuestar. El gasto militar no deja de crecer, las carreras tecnológicas y armamentísticas se intensifican, y cada vez más países se plantean si deberían dotarse de un arsenal nuclear disuasorio que garantice su seguridad.

In a recent development, no hay nada más peligroso que normalizar la guerra. Supone regresar a una norma que imperó durante la mayor parte de la historia de la humanidad. La guerra era el eje vertebrador del sistema internacional. Era la vía natural por la que los Estados zanjaban sus disputas o ensanchaban su territorio a costa de vecinos más débiles.

Pero la inmensa devastación que produjeron las dos guerras mundiales en la primera mitad del siglo XX hizo inaceptable ese statu quo. Los países se unieron en un empeño común: que la guerra dejara de ser un instrumento legítimo de la política de Estado y pasara a ser un acto ilegal. Las guerras no terminaron en 1945, pero durante años la comunidad internacional las condenó de forma abrumadora.

En las últimas décadas, sin embargo, el compromiso de los gobiernos con la causa de la paz se ha debilitado. En 2003, millones de personas salieron a las calles en cientos de ciudades para oponerse a la invasión de Irak liderada por Estados Unidos. Y, aun así, la guerra siguió adelante. Iniciada a partir de premisas falsas y en violación del derecho internacional, arrasó Irak, agravó la inestabilidad regional y avivó el resentimiento y el terrorismo contra los países occidentales. Aquel conflicto marcó, además, un punto de inflexión. Desde entonces, la búsqueda de la paz ha ido retrocediendo en la agenda internacional, arrinconada por la creciente competencia geopolítica y la desatención o la indiferencia hacia los esfuerzos multilaterales que durante décadas pusieron freno a la guerra.

According to recent reports, este camino conduce a una nueva guerra mundial: la catástrofe que el orden del siglo XX se propuso evitar. Ante ese futuro sombrío en el horizonte, los gobiernos deben reaprender el arte de oponerse a la guerra. Todos los países, incluido el mío, España, tienen la responsabilidad de actuar para limitar la capacidad de otros de librar la guerra y para fortalecer las instituciones internacionales que han de ser garantes de la paz.

According to recent reports, el éxito de este proyecto dependerá de un multilateralismo expansivo, al que yo llamo «maxilateralismo»: una cooperación que abarque al mayor número posible de países, en lugar de limitarse a pequeñas coaliciones ad hoc. Su ambición es que la guerra resulte cada vez más inviable, incluso inimaginable. En 2003, manifestantes por toda España coreaban «¡No a la guerra!». En 2026, el mundo no puede volver a ignorarlos.

Industry observers note that los esfuerzos internacionales por desterrar la guerra como instrumento de política nacional se remontan al Pacto Briand-Kellogg de 1928, un tratado firmado en París por 15 países, al que posteriormente se sumaron decenas más. No bastó para impedir la Segunda Guerra Mundial, pero plantó una semilla. Cuando representantes de 50 países se reunieron en San Francisco en 1945 para crear las Naciones Unidas, recuperaron el espíritu y los principios del Pacto y añadieron lo que había faltado: estructura institucional. La Carta de Naciones Unidas prohibió recurrir a la amenaza o al uso de la fuerza contra la integridad territorial o la independencia política de otro Estado. Y, a diferencia de su predecesor de 1928, respaldó esa prohibición con instituciones facultadas para hacerla cumplir.

En las décadas siguientes, estas instituciones levantaron un orden que castigaba las violaciones al derecho internacional e incentivaba la cooperación y la diplomacia. Al mismo tiempo, el rechazo popular a la guerra y al militarismo de la Guerra Fría cobraba fuerza en todo el mundo. Se hizo visible en la resistencia a la guerra de Vietnam y en los movimientos de masas contra las armas nucleares. El pacifismo alcanzó su punto álgido en los años noventa, cuando una sociedad civil global pujante se movilizó en defensa de causas humanitarias y Naciones Unidas tenía autoridad para abanderar una ambiciosa agenda de paz.

Industry observers note that hoy, sin embargo, hay más conflictos armados que en ningún otro momento desde 1946. Según el Programa de Datos sobre Conflictos de Uppsala, en 2025 hubo 65 conflictos activos con participación estatal, el doble que en 2010. Se calcula que en estos conflictos murieron 250.000 personas: la cifra anual más alta desde el genocidio de Ruanda hace más de 30 años. Cerca de 120 millones de personas en todo el mundo siguen desplazadas por la guerra.

Y lo más inquietante: las guerras de agresión, que violan la Carta de Naciones Unidas, están de vuelta. Rusia invadió Ucrania. Estados Unidos e Israel atacaron Irán. Y mientras los combates se prolongan año tras año en lugares como el Líbano, Sudán o Yemen, resulta evidente que la guerra está siendo aceptada de nuevo como algo normal.

According to recent reports, nada indica que esta tendencia vaya a frenarse. Los presupuestos militares se han disparado hasta niveles no vistos en generaciones, en detrimento del gasto social y de desarrollo. Solo en la última década, el gasto mundial en defensa ha aumentado más de un 40 %, y muchos países han duplicado sus presupuestos militares. Los casi 3 billones de dólares que el mundo destina cada año a defensa se acercan al producto interior bruto de todo el continente africano. Incluso países con una larga tradición de contención militar, como Alemania, Dinamarca, Japón y Noruega, se están rearmando a toda velocidad, y algunos están recuperando el servicio militar.

According to recent reports, aún más estremecedor es el regreso de la amenaza de guerra nuclear. Los nueve Estados con armas nucleares están modernizando sus arsenales y aumentando su capacidad destructiva. Se calcula que el arsenal de China ha pasado de entre unas 200-300 cabezas nucleares a finales de la década de 2010 a 620 este año. Corea del Norte también ha ampliado el suyo, de entre 10-20 cabezas estimadas en 2018 a unas 60 este año, y ha desarrollado plataformas de lanzamiento cada vez más sofisticadas. En marzo, Francia anunció el primer aumento de su número de cabezas nucleares desde 1992. Estados Unidos y Rusia, las dos mayores potencias nucleares del mundo, no han sido capaces de preservar el último tratado que ponía límites a sus arsenales estratégicos. Y cada vez más potencias no nucleares han empezado a plantearse adquirir armas nucleares propias.

According to recent reports, al mismo tiempo, la inteligencia artificial (IA) está dotando a la guerra de armas cada vez más peligrosas. La supervisión humana se reduce progresivamente a medida que la IA permite automatizar ciberataques contra redes eléctricas, hospitales y sistemas financieros. Hay sistemas de IA que ya han logrado infiltrarse en organismos públicos y han hecho posible la producción masiva de deepfakes y de campañas de desinformación.

La integración de la IA en las tecnologías nucleares es una amenaza existencial: al acelerar la toma de decisiones, comprime el tiempo disponible para el juicio humano. Del mismo modo, el uso de la IA en biotecnología podría rebajar drásticamente las barreras a la experimentación nociva y al desarrollo de armas biológicas. En ambos terrenos, esta tecnología está elevando a niveles sin precedentes el riesgo de errores de cálculo, de escaladas involuntarias y de destrucción masiva.

According to recent reports, en conjunto, estas dinámicas multiplican las probabilidades de que cualquier crisis desemboque rápidamente en la aniquilación del planeta. Por desgracia, los países están fabricando los instrumentos de la catástrofe a la velocidad vertiginosa de la innovación, mientras que los instrumentos de control avanzan al ritmo, mucho más lento, de la diplomacia.

Los cambios políticos están alejando al mundo de la paz. Lo empujan hacia la militarización y la confrontación. Un mundo multipolar no es, por definición, más peligroso. Pero la erosión de las normas y de las instituciones que deberían encauzar las tensiones entre los distintos polos está provocando que el mundo se vuelva especialmente volátil. La competencia entre grandes potencias se intensifica: las ansias de hegemonía alientan políticas exteriores agresivas y los Estados revisionistas desafían las normas y las fronteras establecidas. El nacionalismo beligerante crece. Los movimientos de extrema derecha promueven una visión del mundo en la que las relaciones internacionales son un juego de suma cero y los países deben competir en lugar de cooperar. Incluso dirigentes de centro están adoptando la retórica de la guerra. Aunque no pretendan iniciar una, sus palabras abonan una mentalidad militarista peligrosa.

In a recent development, en este clima de rivalidad, las guerras de agresión se envuelven en discursos de necesidad, liberación, legítima defensa o justicia histórica. Los agresores presentan sus operaciones como inevitables, después de haber demonizado a sus adversarios para justificar un ataque preventivo. Venden cada guerra como la respuesta a la inseguridad: la guerra que acabará con todas las guerras.

Pero estas guerras no harán del mundo un lugar más seguro. Cada vez que un Estado desata una guerra de agresión, erosiona las normas que protegen a todos los países frente al uso arbitrario de la fuerza, incluido el propio Estado agresor.

In a recent development, las guerras tienen un coste inmenso. Destrozan sociedades y truncan vidas. En 2025, según los registros de Naciones Unidas, al menos un civil murió en conflicto armado cada 14 minutos, y más de cinco millones de personas se vieron obligadas a huir de sus países. El coste económico también es altísimo. La guerra que enfrenta a Estados Unidos e Israel con Irán ha alterado gravemente el comercio marítimo y el tráfico aéreo y ha disparado los precios de la energía, los fertilizantes y otras materias primas. Millones de personas en todo el mundo están sufriendo las consecuencias.

It has been revealed that la guerra genera, además, nuevos peligros. Una vez que empiezan los combates, su rumbo es imprevisible. Los conflictos tienden a arrastrar a nuevos actores y a desbordarse hacia los países vecinos. La guerra de Irán vuelve a ser un ejemplo claro. Desde febrero de 2026, Irán ha atacado objetivos en varios países del Golfo y de su entorno, acciones que España ha condenado sin excepción. Los ataques contra buques civiles y mercantes amenazan la estabilidad del conjunto de la región. Y la guerra ha reavivado los conflictos de Irak, el Líbano y Yemen.

In a recent development, por último, las guerras rara vez traen una paz duradera. Al contrario: ahondan los agravios y enquistan las divisiones que alimentan la violencia del mañana. La guerra de Rusia en Ucrania, por ejemplo, ha dinamitado la confianza en Moscú. El genocidio en Gaza ha exacerbado la indignación contra Israel, y eso podría desembocar en nuevas oleadas de terrorismo. Y la guerra contra Irán ha desestabilizado aún más la región y ha lastrado la cooperación entre sus países.

El mundo tiene la responsabilidad de resistirse a la normalización de la guerra. Callar es un acto de cobardía y de complicidad. La sociedad española está dejando clara su posición: tres de cada cuatro españoles señalan la guerra como su mayor temor. Y un número aún mayor cree que se cierne otra guerra mundial.

Pero no basta con condenar la guerra en abstracto. La ambición de acabar con ella debe ir acompañada de acciones concretas que hagan cada vez más difícil que los países inicien, sostengan y justifiquen un conflicto armado.

Sources indicate that españa ha procurado actuar en esa dirección. Ha defendido las normas internacionales que marcan la diferencia entre un orden basado en reglas y otro gobernado por la fuerza. Y ha denunciado siempre los ataques armados que violan la Carta de Naciones Unidas.

Desde el primer día de la guerra en Gaza, España ha reclamado un alto el fuego inmediato y permanente, la liberación de todos los rehenes y la entrada sin restricciones de la ayuda humanitaria. En mayo de 2024, España reconoció el Estado de Palestina con la esperanza de que este paso contribuyera a avanzar hacia una solución negociada y duradera del conflicto. Y ha apoyado activamente los esfuerzos de la Corte Internacional de Justicia y de la Corte Penal Internacional para que los dirigentes israelíes rindan cuentas por sus violaciones del derecho internacional humanitario. Israel tenía derecho a la legítima defensa tras los atentados terroristas del 7 de octubre. Pero ese derecho no justifica el genocidio en Gaza ni la expansión de la ocupación ilegal de Cisjordania.

According to recent reports, disuadir la guerra exige también elevar el coste de la agresión. El resto del mundo debe asegurarse de que quien elija hacer la guerra no pueda hacerlo sin pagar un precio. A lo largo de la invasión rusa de Ucrania, por ejemplo, la Unión Europea ha aprobado sucesivas rondas de sanciones contra Rusia que España ha respaldado sin titubeos. España también ha prestado a Ucrania ayuda financiera, humanitaria y militar para que pueda defender su territorio y negarle a Rusia el botín de guerra.

Los países deben negarse a ayudar a las partes a extender los conflictos en curso. España, por ejemplo, mantiene un embargo de armas a Israel desde 2023. Este año, además, negó a Estados Unidos el uso de su territorio y de sus instalaciones para la guerra contra Irán. La decisión de España no fue un acto de hostilidad hacia un aliado. Tampoco fue una expresión de neutralidad ni de simpatía hacia el régimen iraní. Fue el fruto de una valoración estratégica: implicarse habría favorecido la escalada del conflicto y agravado la inseguridad regional y mundial. Para ser fiel a su compromiso con la paz, España tenía que estar dispuesta a decir no, aunque eso tuviera un coste político. Si más países hubieran actuado igual, las guerras de Gaza y de Irán habrían sido mucho más difíciles y costosas de librar.

Industry observers note that invertir en prosperidad es igualmente esencial. La seguridad crece cuando las sociedades son resilientes, las desigualdades se reducen y la ciudadanía puede confiar en las instituciones públicas. La decisión de España, el año pasado, de no asumir el objetivo de gasto en defensa del 5 % del PIB propuesto por la OTAN refleja esta visión. No nace de una falta de compromiso con la defensa europea. De hecho, mi Gobierno ha sido uno de los principales impulsores de la autonomía estratégica de la Unión Europea, triplicando el gasto neto en defensa en los ocho años que llevo en el cargo. Pero la disuasión militar y el bienestar social deben reforzarse mutuamente. Al mantener un gasto en defensa proporcionado, España ha conservado el margen fiscal necesario para invertir 145.000 millones de euros adicionales en protección social, vivienda, sanidad y educación, y más de 30.000 millones en la transición ecológica. Son políticas que cohesionan la sociedad y, por tanto, la hacen más segura.

Los esfuerzos de un solo país tienen, sin embargo, un alcance limitado. Cortarle el oxígeno a la guerra exige la implicación de todos: un esfuerzo colectivo basado en un multilateralismo genuino. Esta es la única estrategia que ha funcionado en el pasado. El sistema multilateral construido tras la Segunda Guerra Mundial abarcaba todo el planeta y contribuyó a preservar la paz entre las grandes potencias y a evitar una tercera guerra mundial.

Reforzarlo no será tarea fácil. La pugna geopolítica y una desconfianza generalizada han debilitado a Naciones Unidas, los organismos financieros internacionales, las organizaciones regionales y otras instituciones multilaterales. Muchos países las perciben como ineficaces y atrapadas en una crisis perpetua, de modo que están recurriendo a marcos alternativos para intentar poner fin a las guerras.

Algunos han optado por enfoques unilaterales, persiguiendo acuerdos transaccionales que acaban beneficiando a élites económicas y políticas y dejan al margen a las poblaciones afectadas por el conflicto. Los altos el fuego o los acuerdos de paz que logran pueden ser preferibles a la continuación de la guerra, pero cualquier paz impuesta por la ley del más fuerte, y no por el derecho, se asienta sobre cimientos frágiles.

Otros países, frustrados con el multilateralismo, han intentado formar «coaliciones de voluntarios» u otros grupos «minilaterales» para garantizar su seguridad o alcanzar acuerdos ad hoc en materia de comercio o tecnología. Este enfoque puede ser una solución temporal a la parálisis de las instituciones tradicionales, pero su carácter excluyente fragmenta aún más un orden internacional ya dividido. Lo que necesitamos no es minilateralismo, sino maxilateralismo. La cooperación internacional alcanza su verdadera fuerza cuando es—o aspira a ser—universal. Dejar a una parte del mundo fuera de estos esfuerzos es, además, incubar la confrontación de mañana.

Industry observers note that el sistema internacional del siglo XX no era perfecto. Sus normas se han aplicado de manera desigual, sus principios se han defendido de forma inconsistente y sus procedimientos han sido desesperantemente lentos. Pero es innegable que, sin él, el mundo sería un polvorín aún mayor. Basta un ejemplo: fue una red de tratados internacionales—entre ellos, el Tratado sobre la No Proliferación de las Armas Nucleares, el Tratado sobre Fuerzas Nucleares de Alcance Intermedio y el Tratado de Prohibición Parcial de los Ensayos Nucleares—la que puso fin a una carrera armamentística desbocada y extraordinariamente costosa que estaba llevando al mundo al borde de una guerra nuclear.

According to recent reports, toda esta arquitectura institucional se está resquebrajando. Y sin ella, aspirar a preservar la paz es una quimera.

Fortalecer las instituciones multilaterales debe ser el eje central de una campaña global para relegar la guerra a los libros de historia. Para ello será necesario acometer reformas de calado que les devuelvan la legitimidad y refuercen su capacidad de actuación, dando prioridad a las medidas que más contribuyan a la paz y la seguridad.

La primera pasa por aumentar la representación en las Naciones Unidas y las instituciones de Bretton Woods. Actualizar la estructura del Consejo de Seguridad de Naciones Unidas es especialmente importante, dada su responsabilidad principal de mantener la paz internacional. Un Consejo de Seguridad con asientos permanentes y derecho de veto para las cinco potencias vencedoras de la Segunda Guerra Mundial, que en conjunto suman apenas una cuarta parte de la población mundial, no refleja el mundo de hoy. Debe ampliarse el número de miembros electos del Consejo y alargar su mandato más allá de los dos años actuales. Los nuevos asientos deben otorgarse principalmente a países de regiones infrarrepresentadas, en particular África y América Latina. Organizaciones regionales como la Unión Europea y la Unión Africana también deberían estar representadas en el Consejo, posiblemente ocupando puestos que hoy corresponden a Estados. Un Consejo de Seguridad más representativo no solo sería más justo, sino también más eficaz. Los países defienden y hacen cumplir con más empeño las normas internacionales cuando se sienten autores de ellas.

También hay que restringir estrictamente el poder de veto de los miembros permanentes, en especial cuando el Consejo de Seguridad delibere sobre casos de atrocidades masivas, genocidio, crímenes de lesa humanidad y crímenes de guerra. En última instancia, el veto debe abolirse por completo. Solo entonces podrá el Consejo responder a todos los actos de agresión sin quedar secuestrado por las objeciones de un solo Estado.

Industry observers note that un espíritu similar debería orientar la transformación estructural de las instituciones financieras internacionales, en particular el Fondo Monetario Internacional y el Banco Mundial. La distribución del poder de voto en ambas sigue reflejando los equilibrios económicos del siglo XX y, por convención, un europeo está siempre al frente del FMI y un estadounidense, del Banco Mundial. Esto debe terminar. Las economías emergentes necesitan una representación más adecuada, y los puestos de liderazgo deben estar abiertos a todos los candidatos, sea cual sea su nacionalidad. También deberán evolucionar las responsabilidades que asumen en instituciones como la Organización Mundial del Comercio los países antes considerados «en desarrollo», a medida que crecen y se incorporan al grupo de las economías más ricas. Una gobernanza económica más justa aliviaría la desigualdad y el resentimiento que con tanta frecuencia atizan la inestabilidad y los conflictos.

Recent findings suggest that otra reforma esencial consiste en revitalizar el marco internacional que contiene el riesgo de escalada nuclear. Parte de ese trabajo depende de las potencias nucleares. Corresponde a Estados Unidos y a Rusia negociar un tratado que suceda al acuerdo bilateral Nuevo START y que preserve topes verificables al despliegue de armas nucleares. Y, esta vez, China debería participar en las conversaciones.

Recent findings suggest that pero el esfuerzo más amplio exige el compromiso de todos los países. Entre sus prioridades deben figurar la ratificación del Tratado de Prohibición Completa de los Ensayos Nucleares, para impedir que se reanuden las pruebas nucleares, y el avance de las negociaciones sobre un Tratado de Prohibición de la Producción de Material Fisionable, que prohibiría la producción de uranio altamente enriquecido y plutonio para armas nucleares. Todos deben también trabajar conjuntamente para regular el uso de la IA en el ámbito militar, especialmente en lo que respecta a las armas nucleares, a fin de preservar el control humano sobre las decisiones de lanzamiento y minimizar el riesgo de errores fatales. Los países no nucleares deben comprometerse a no adquirir armas nucleares y deben emplear todos los medios a su alcance para instar a las potencias nucleares a reducir sus arsenales, reforzar los mecanismos de verificación y reconstruir las salvaguardas diplomáticas que durante décadas han ayudado a evitar una catástrofe nuclear.

Industry observers note that la tecnología puede contribuir en parte a esta tarea. Los avances en imágenes por satélite, sensores remotos y análisis de datos pueden aumentar la transparencia y la supervisión del cumplimiento de los acuerdos de control de armamentos. Pero también hay que hacer mucho más para evitar situaciones que puedan precipitar una guerra. Si los Estados con armas nucleares acuerdan reducir su disponibilidad operacional y reforzar la comunicación en momentos de tensión, los gobiernos contarán con más tiempo y más medios para desactivar las crisis. Cada país debe proteger sus sistemas de mando y control frente a los ciberataques y la manipulación informativa impulsada por la IA, de modo que una falsa alarma o un error de cálculo no desencadenen jamás una guerra nuclear.

Por último, es prioritario trabajar para garantizar que el sistema de justicia internacional pueda hacer cumplir las decisiones de los tribunales. Desmantelar la Corte Penal Internacional, como pretenden algunos países, solo aseguraría la impunidad de los crímenes más atroces. La CPI no solo debe investigar y juzgar los casos de genocidio, agresión, crímenes de guerra y crímenes de lesa humanidad, sino también contar con la autoridad necesaria para llevar ante la justicia a los responsables de esos crímenes. Cuando un Estado pasa a ser parte del Estatuto de Roma, el tratado que creó la CPI, acepta someterse a la jurisdicción de la Corte. Sin embargo, si ese Estado se niega a cooperar o a entregar a un sospechoso, no existe una sanción efectiva, sino apenas una llamada de atención. Esto debe cambiar. Los Estados que den cobijo a personas imputadas por la CPI deben afrontar consecuencias legales, diplomáticas y financieras. Iniciar y librar una guerra debe tener un coste real.

La reforma de las instituciones internacionales lleva años estancada, pero la próxima elección para la Secretaría General de Naciones Unidas ofrece una ocasión excepcional para darle un nuevo impulso. Que Naciones Unidas nombrara a su primera secretaria general sería un poderoso símbolo de renovación, inclusión y adaptación institucional. La organización no puede afirmar verdaderamente que habla en nombre de toda la humanidad mientras no la haya dirigido una mujer. Alcanzar este hito podría despertar una nueva ambición y reforzar la confianza en la capacidad de las instituciones internacionales para reformarse y para que recuperen su papel a la hora de poner freno a la guerra.

Frenar la deriva del mundo hacia la guerra exigirá el compromiso más amplio posible. Ningún país, grande o pequeño, puede mirar hacia otro lado ni sumarse a las acciones que aviven la escalada. Todos debemos defender las normas internacionales que hoy ponen coto a la guerra y reformar y dotar de poder a las instituciones que mañana la harán imposible.

In a recent development, en última instancia, lo que hará inimaginable la guerra es una agenda de paz positiva que aborde las causas profundas de la inseguridad. Cada paso hacia la erradicación de la pobreza, la ampliación del acceso a una educación de calidad, el avance de la igualdad de género, el fortalecimiento de las instituciones democráticas y el aumento de la resiliencia ante los desastres naturales atenúa también las condiciones que engendran la violencia.

Industry observers note that las instituciones financieras internacionales deben ser capaces de proporcionar financiación con rapidez, a gran escala y a un coste razonable, para que ningún país en desarrollo se vea obligado a elegir entre atender su deuda e invertir en su población. Los bancos multilaterales de desarrollo deben poder movilizar fondos para las transiciones ecológica y digital, de modo que las migraciones climáticas y la disputa por los recursos no se conviertan en detonantes de conflictos entre Estados. Y el Acuerdo sobre Pandemias de la Organización Mundial de la Salud debe ultimarse y entrar en vigor para garantizar que todos los países puedan acceder a vacunas y tratamientos cuando llegue la próxima emergencia sanitaria mundial.

Recent findings suggest that por eso España ha procurado situar el desarrollo en el centro de su política exterior. El Gobierno español ha sido un firme defensor de los Objetivos de Desarrollo Sostenible de la ONU para 2030 y, el año pasado, la ciudad de Sevilla acogió la Cuarta Conferencia Internacional sobre la Financiación para el Desarrollo, donde la comunidad internacional se comprometió a aligerar la carga de la deuda de los países vulnerables y a desbloquear inversiones para el desarrollo sostenible. España también ha promovido iniciativas como el Centro Global para Canjes de Deuda por Desarrollo, lanzado junto con el Banco Mundial; la Alianza multilateral por las Cláusulas de Suspensión de Deuda, que permite a los países vulnerables suspender el pago de su deuda tras una catástrofe; y un mecanismo propio para ofrecer hasta 60 millones de euros anuales en alivio de deuda a países en desarrollo. Además, España ha respaldado, junto con instituciones multilaterales y organizaciones internacionales, iniciativas de financiación climática, salud global, igualdad de género, seguridad alimentaria y protección social. Estas políticas de desarrollo son también políticas de construcción de paz.

Industry observers note that un proyecto ambicioso de movilización global en favor del derecho internacional y de un multilateralismo genuino puede parecer poco realista. Pero ya hemos visto lo que ocurre cuando la normalización de la guerra arrastra a la humanidad al infierno. Los hombres y las mujeres que se levantaron de entre las ruinas de la Segunda Guerra Mundial, el capítulo más oscuro de nuestra historia, encontraron la manera de construir un orden mundial multilateral. La pregunta a la que se enfrenta nuestra generación es si seremos capaces de preservar el imperio de la ley o permitiremos el regreso de la ley de la jungla. Si construiremos el mundo del mañana con visión de futuro y cooperación, o a través del caos y del dolor de otra guerra mundial. Debemos elegir bien mientras la decisión siga estando en nuestras manos.

Marco Rubio's 2028 stock surges among House Republicans as Trump insiders split on Vance

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hurt examines the speculation surrounding Trump's potential successor, the political futures of Vance and Rubio and what the president's comments could mean for the Republican Party's leadership heading into 2028.

As Republicans continue to pick up the pieces from their 2026 midterm losses, one Trump administration official is catching some GOP lawmakers' eyes as the party's next great hope.

According to recent reports, "[Secretary of State Marco Rubio] is the whole package. He's intelligent, charismatic, level-headed, cool-tempered and very knowledgeable about the challenges and eloquent in explaining them," Rep. Nicole Malliotakis, R-N.Y., told Fox News Digital. "I think there is a lot of interest from Republicans in seeing him explore a run.".

Industry observers note that indeed, multiple House Republicans who spoke with Fox News Digital noted they and their colleagues are pushing Rubio to run for president in 2028. The Cabinet official himself has publicly dismissed any talk about his future political plans, but his name is on the rise among Republicans who have said the party needs to pivot from the issues that cost them votes in November.

HOUSE CONSERVATIVE EMERGES WITH 2028 PRESIDENTIAL PICK AFTER GOP'S MIDTERM MASSACRE: 'I AM ALL IN'.

Recent findings suggest that "Now that we lost majorities, we can't push policy, so we will have to do better at communicating," Rep. Marlin Stutzman, R-Ind., told Fox News Digital on election night. "I am all in for Marco. He can be a unifier.".

Industry observers note that secretary of State Marco Rubio holds his end-of-year press conference at the State Department in Washington, D.C., Dec. 19, 2025. (Kevin Mohatt/Reuters).

They're notable comments coming from the Indiana Republican, who was among the founding members of the conservative House Freedom Caucus.

MAGA VOTERS REVEAL WHO THEY WANT TO SEE LEAD GOP IN 2028.

Rubio has long been held up as a potential 2028 contender, despite a previous unsuccessful White House bid in 2016.

He and Vice President JD Vance have been regarded as the top contenders for the GOP nomination, but it's Rubio's name that has come up in conversations among House Republicans, Fox News Digital was told.

GOP MIDTERM BLOODBATH EXPOSES CRACKS IN VANCE'S 2028 WHITE HOUSE AMBITIONS.

"A number of my colleagues, unsolicited by me — they come up with me, knowing that I'm on board, [from] Miami, et cetera — and said that they'd want to support him, that they would support him if he ran," Rep. Carlos Gimenez, R-Fla., told Fox News Digital. " And it's not just a few. There's a number, a pretty good number, that have told me that.".

According to recent reports, secretary of State Marco Rubio speaks at the Pnyx hill, where ancient Athenians held democratic assemblies, with the ancient Parthenon temple atop the Acropolis seen in the background, in Athens on Oct. 7, 2026. (Mark Schiefelbein/AFP via Getty Images).

According to recent reports, gimenez noted he supported Rubio even before the election. The same goes for Rep. Mike Haridopolos, R-Fla., who told Fox News Digital he's been openly backing his fellow Florida Republican for two months.

"And I think the affirmation that I'm getting from talking to people is overwhelming," Haridopolos stated.

"He is not only understanding what's happening today, but our place in history. And I think his inspirational story, his parents coming from Cuba and living the opportunity that is America, and inspiring people that anything is possible is the uplifting message we need.".

SEC MARCO RUBIO: THE WEST FORGOT WHAT MADE IT GREAT. WE MUST REDISCOVER OUR ROOTS BEFORE WE LOSE THEM.

Recent findings suggest that both Haridopolos and Malliotakis pointed to Rubio's recent speech in Greece calling for the renewal of Western civilization as an example of his presidential possibility. Those remarks, set in Athens, were widely lauded for their scenic backdrop of the Acropolis at sunset.

And Malliotakis, who is half Cuban herself, said Rubio could "reach" Hispanic voters who largely turned away from the GOP in November.

LATINO VOTERS SWING BACK TO DEMOCRATS AHEAD OF MIDTERM ELECTIONS: POLL.

"The potential for him to be the first Hispanic president is huge for our party and the country," she said.

President Donald Trump reacts as he speaks to the media as he arrives at Glasgow Prestwick Airport on July 25, 2025, in Prestwick, Scotland. (Andrew Harnik/Getty Images).

But within the administration itself, it appears no clear successor has emerged.

One source familiar with talks told Fox News Digital that Trump administration staffers were "about 50/50" when asked if they favored Vance or Rubio.

Sources indicate that "I think it’s pretty split," one administration official mentioned. "I don’t think the president really knows. I think if you asked him today, he’d say Rubio.".

"50/50 feels right to me," a second administration official said.

White House spokeswoman Anna Kelly referred Fox News Digital to President Donald Trump’s previous comments on the matter.

Over the weekend, Trump told Fox News' "Saturday in America" that Vance and Rubio are "doing fantastically" and are "both very, very popular" when asked who he would like to see run on the Republican and Democratic tickets ahead of the 2028 presidential election.
